current.text: Yahoo lists him as questionable with a toe injury.
Murray, Trey Murphy and Zion Williamson are locked into the Pelicans starting lineup. Jeremiah Fears does not take his starting spot.
He should start the season with no minutes limit and is not expected to sit back-to-backs.
He is projected for about 33 minutes and 25 percent usage. Experts expect more minutes and better shooting than last season.
Experts agree he is undervalued. They call an ADP around 67 to 70 too low and like him as a round 4 pick. One expert drafted him in round 3, and one sees him as a top 30 to 35 player.
In an expert auction mock he went for 24 USD. The bidder who targeted him hoped to pay 15 or 16 USD and stopped at 23 USD.
He turned 70% of his deflections into steals last season. If that rate drops, more minutes may not bring more steals.
The Pelicans have a crowded rotation and a new coach, Jamahl Mosley, so roles are hard to project. Murray's starting spot is not in question.
Experts see New Orleans as a weak team near the bottom of the West, at about 34 wins. One expert does not expect them to give up on the season.

durable.text: He tore his Achilles and came back last season for about 14 games on limited minutes.
Turnovers are his clearly weak category. They are well worse than the league pool and weak even for a guard.
Steals are his best category, and he could be a two-steals player.
He is not a lights-out shooter. He can make threes but does not space the floor.
For a good guard defender, he turns few contests into blocks: 5.3% last season against a career rate of 8 to 9%. A small rise is possible.

note: The markets price him cheaply: 3.2 USD average cost on Yahoo and 7.8 USD on ESPN. Yahoo values him at 18 USD and experts call him a round 4 value, so expect a real bidding war, like the 24 USD he went for in a mock auction. He gives steals, assists and rebounds for a guard, but his 3.2 turnovers per game make him a natural fit for punt TO builds. He hurts any team that competes in TO. Early in the season, check that the toe (Yahoo Q) does not cost games, that he plays about 33 minutes with no limit, and that his steals hold up.
